final.title: What contact decay hides in a small business
final.body:
Contact decay is not usually a big strategy problem. In a 1-10 person business, it is the point where a lead, customer, or supplier contact has gone quiet and nobody notices until the work has already slipped away. That can happen in a CRM, an inbox, or a spreadsheet that looks tidy right up until you need it. The issue is visibility: if you do not know which contacts have gone stale, you cannot tell whether you have a sales problem, a process problem, or just a memory problem. Human memory is a brave little filing system.

For an owner, the practical decision is simple: do not start by automating everything. Start by checking one week of your contact list and marking every record you already know went dormant. Then note how you found out: a missed reply, an old quote, a customer who never came back, or a note discovered too late. That gives you a clean boundary. If your work already lives in digital tools and the quiet contacts are easy to spot once you look, a lightweight flag may be worth building. If most contacts arrive by phone or walk-in, AI may not be the right fit.

Once you can see which contacts have gone quiet and why, you know whether a simple system to flag them is worth building.

final.title: What contact decay hides in a small business
final.body:
Contact decay is not usually a grand strategy problem. In a 1-10 person business, it is the quiet moment when a lead, customer, or supplier contact goes stale and nobody notices until the opportunity has already slipped. That can happen in a CRM, an inbox, or a spreadsheet with tidy columns and no follow-up discipline. The real issue is visibility: if you do not know which contacts have gone quiet, you do not know whether you have a sales problem, a process problem, or just a memory problem. Then write down how you noticed each one: missed reply, old quote, customer who never came back, or a note you found too late. Once you can see which contacts have gone quiet and why, you will know whether this is a real workflow cost or just background noise.
